anchor_definition: The anchor is the phone-login submit handler (the useCallback bound to _): its body reads e.password/e.mobile, derives a nonce i=F.dnGetter(), computes s=G().ne(nonce+password, d()(mobile.slice(3)+nonce)) and posts {mobile, data:s, time:i}. The encrypted data value is constructed inline here, so this enclosing callback is the anchor; not the imported cipher/hash helpers, not sibling QR login renders, and not modal/container UI wrappers. The immediately enclosing phone-login component is target-specific but broader than the value-building callback, so it receives 0.7.

primary_anchor.why: The memoized phone-login submit callback. Builds s = G().ne(nonce+password, key=d()(mobile.slice(3)+nonce)) and calls x.byPhoneNumber({mobile, data:s, time}). This constructs the exact encrypted data value sent in the login request.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: The memoized phone-login submit callback. Builds s = G().ne(nonce+password, key=d()(mobile.slice(3)+nonce)) and calls x.byPhoneNumber({mobile, data:s, time}). This constructs the exact encrypted data value sent in the login request.

The phone-login component owns the form and contains the anchor useCallback. It is target-specific and would reach the right behavior, but it also renders validation/UI and QR-switch controls, so it is broader than the exact value-building callback.
Reusable MD5 wrapper called as d()(mobile.slice(3)+nonce) to derive the key material for G().ne. It hashes bytes but does not read the form or bind the result to the login data field.
Reusable MD5 digest implementation beneath the exported hash function. It performs generic block hashing and has no phone-login semantics.
Generic MD5 round helper used by the digest primitive. It is core crypto support, not the field-binding login logic.
Generic MD5 round helper used by the digest primitive. It is below the key derivation call and target-independent.
Generic MD5 round helper used by the digest primitive. It contributes to hashing but not to request-field assembly.
Generic MD5 round helper used by the digest primitive. It is reusable crypto internals, not the anchor.
Handles the response of x.byPhoneNumber after the request data has already been constructed and submitted. It is on the request path but not a value constructor.
Login container that switches between QR and phone login and renders the phone component. It is an upstream UI wrapper, not the encrypted data builder.
Switches the login container into the phone-login branch that contains the anchor. It is path-critical UI state, not encryption logic.
Post-login container callback that records analytics and closes/binds UI after a login result. It receives an already completed login outcome.
The WeChat official-account QR login component in the same chunk. It calls loginWechart/loginWechartQr and does not read the password or construct the phone-login data field.
Top-level modal shell for login UI. It wraps login components but does not read phone/password, derive the key, run the cipher, or assemble the data request field.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The exact anchor is the _ callback because the password/mobile reads, nonce derivation, MD5 key derivation, G().ne cipher call and x.byPhoneNumber({data:s}) request are all inline there.
J is target-specific but too broad: it contains the anchor plus form rendering, validators and QR-switch UI, so it is 0.7.
The imported hash/cipher/nonce helpers are reusable primitives and stay below the field-binding anchor.
Login containers, branch-switch callbacks, response callbacks and close handlers are path wrappers and should not outrank the anchor.
QR-code/WeChat login and modal-only UI code are off-chain decoys for this password-derived data observable.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.
